subject: SIG: Request for wrap provenance & rotation sampling (transit)
messages:
From: Aisha Patel <security@novapay.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: infosec@novapay.com
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: SIG: request for transit key wrapping provenance & rotation sampling

Markus —

As part of our SIG assessment for Redwood, our auditors have asked for evidence around transit key wrapping provenance and a sampling of rotation operations for tenant-wrapped keys. High level asks below; target delivery 2027-01-02 (two weeks):

1) Wrap provenance logs: a sampled extract of key wrap/unwrap operations for tenant-wrapped keys covering the last 90 days. Prefer CSV with columns: timestamp, key_id (pseudonymized), operation (wrap/unwrap), wrapping_key_id, caller_identity, request_id, result_code.

2) Rotation sampling: a short rotation timeline (past 6 months) for tenant wrapping keys with timestamps of rotation events, responsible role, and confirmation of key states (active/retired).

3) HSM/vendor attestations: any signed metadata or chain evidence from the HSM vendor showing the key origins and that wrap operations were performed within the FIPS-certified HSM boundary.

4) Config snapshot: algorithm/format used for wrapping (e.g., RSA-OAEP-256 or AES-GCM-wrap), key lengths, and any wrapping policy (expiry, exportability).

Notes: We understand some fields will need redaction for tenant privacy — please pseudonymize keys and caller ids, but preserve the ability to link wrap->rotation events for sampling. If you have a short guidance note on how samples were drawn that would help.

Attachments acceptable as CSV/PDF/TXT. If you expect vendor-signed artifacts to take longer, please flag the expected ETA.

Thanks — appreciate a quick confirmation of scope and ETA.

—Aisha
Aisha Patel
Senior Security Analyst, NovaPay
security@novapay.com

From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 14:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: SIG: request for transit key wrapping provenance & rotation sampling

Markus —

We can cover the CSV extract and rotation timeline. Quick plan and artifacts to deliver by 2027-01-02: 

1) wrap_log_samples_202609-202612.csv (attached) — 90-day sampled extract, 4,800 rows, pseudonymized key_id->KID_xxx mapping preserved in a separate mapping file (attached as mapping_notes.txt). Columns: timestamp, pseudo_key_id, operation, wrapping_key_id, caller_tag, request_id, result_code. We include a short sampling note header in the CSV.

2) rotation_plan_summary_2026-12-19.pdf (attached) — condensed rotation timeline (6 months) showing rotation events, role owner, and verification checks.

3) hsm_vendor_signature_chain.txt (attached) — vendor-signed metadata we received from our HSM partner listing the origin of wrapping keys and a signed timestamp for key import events. The vendor sig is in PKCS7 text form. (Note: vendor asked that raw signing certs not be published broadly; the TXT contains the signed assertion only.)

4) wrapped-key-export-sample.bin.sha256.txt — SHA256 checksum of a small wrapped-key export sample, to satisfy the auditor checksum ask without sharing raw wrapped key material.

Masking approach: we replaced tenant IDs with tenant_###, and used consistent pseudonyms for key identifiers so reviewers can link wrap events to subsequent rotation events without seeing tenant PII. Request_ids are intact.

If they need additional evidence (e.g., HSM serial numbers or attestation PDFs) I can escalate to our vendor contact; expect a 3–5 business day lag for that.

Deliverables attached here; letting you review before I send to Aisha.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: wrap_log_samples_202609-202612.csv (CSV stub), rotation_plan_summary_2026-12-19.pdf (PDF stub), hsm_vendor_signature_chain.txt (TXT stub), wrapped-key-export-sample.bin.sha256.txt (TXT stub)
